title: Henri IV to Andre Hurault de Maisse, ambassador at Venice, 3 and 7 November 1592, in Maisse's Cipher (1592) (BnF fr. 16093 ff. 370, 373)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16093 f. 370 (ark btv1b90074656, canvas 419; old Harlay ms. 1024 piece 224)

plaintext.source: Contemporary clerk's copy, fully in clear, BnF NAF 6984 (fonds Brienne 13) fol. 102v, ark btv1b100904592; located through the Harlay piece number in Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives t. III

transcription.source: Gallica scan at native 7029x6142, read at 4.5-6x
transcription.notes: Only the opening of the leaf is transcribed group by group: 80 groups of the roughly 630 on the recto. The rest reads with the same key by spot decoding.

transcription.source: not transcribed; read from the clear copy

system.summary: Maisse's Cipher (1592): a simple substitution on a 22-letter alphabet in figures 1-22, with doubled-letter signs (66, 67, 68, 72, 73), a second sign (omega) for d and a sparse nomenclator above the band.

diacritics.note: Overbars on the leaf mark ordinary scribal abbreviation in the plaintext spelling (l[ett]res, occa[si]on), not cipher values; separating dots divide figures.

system.doubled_letters: special sign (ff, mm, nn, ss, uu)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction from the sibling leaves of the same volume (henryiv_Maisse1.png, from f. 317), used; Savasse (1997) reconstructed it independently from the Manuscrit Revol
system.notes: Key: a=7 b=8 c=9 d=10 e=11 f=1 g=2 h=3 i=4 l=5 m=6 n=12 o=13 p=14 q=15 r=16 s=17 u=19 x=20 y=21 z=22; ff=66 mm=67 nn=68 ss=72 uu=73. An omega-shaped sign on f. 370 is a second sign for d and is absent from Tomokiyo's table. ff. 406/410 use a different cipher (maisse1593).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's key for Maisse's Cipher (1592), published as an image on cryptiana and reconstructed from sibling leaves; no reading of ff. 370/373 published; he lists them as undeciphered (no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved), so he may have read them; contemporary clear copies of both letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984), unprinted

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: segmentation and reading aids (seg.py, seg2.py, boxes.py, zoom.py, montage.py)
glyph clustering (glyphs.py, digits.py, cluster.py), left unfinished
blind known-plaintext alignment with a shuffled-cipher control (align.py, align2.py, control.py)

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.
The opening of f. 370 transcribed group by group (80 groups) from the native-resolution scan.

Blind frequency analysis of the transcription: 94% of groups in a contiguous band 1-22, commonest value 14.5%, sparse values above the band - a simple substitution with a small nomenclator, not the assumed homophonic system.

Blind known-plaintext alignment of the transcription against the Brienne clear text placed 12 groups against a shuffled-cipher control of mean 8.2 and p95 11 - at the noise floor, because the transcription mis-split 9 7 as 97 and homophony was wrongly assumed.

The old Harlay piece numbers on the leaves (224, 226 for ff. 370, 373; 247, 251 for the 1593 leaves) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give a clear copy in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 for each; the copies located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's key images fetched from his page (invisible in a text dump); the cipher 1 key (henryiv_Maisse1.png) transcribed to key1.tsv.
The key applied to the 80 transcribed groups of f. 370 and the result normalised against Brienne 13 fol. 102v: 81 of 81 characters identical.
ff. 370 and 373 read from the Brienne clear copies (fol. 102v, 104v).

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from maisse1592, which had joined ff. 370/373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) with ff. 406/410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93, the Breves cipher). This profile keeps ff. 370 and 373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 370: ct370.txt and the decode.py output with the Brienne comparison (texts/f370_decryption.md), opening only; f. 373 has no transcription or decryption in the repository, linked to the Gallica images of the leaf and of the Brienne 13 clear copy.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): texts/f370_decryption.md read: the 80-group opening reads and matches the Brienne copy (reviewed A), but the rest of f. 370 and all of f. 373 are not transcribed, and neither clear copy is in the repository. f. 373 relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 1.0 -> about 0.06 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b29): f. 373r-v fetched at full size (Gallica btv1b90074656 views 422-423, openapi IIIF) and the contemporary clear copy Brienne 13 fol. 104r foot-106v top (btv1b100904592 views 109-112) transcribed in full for the first time (texts/f373_brienne_copy.txt). The copy omits the close and a six-line clear postscript (Joyeuse's defeat at Villemur), read from the original with two lines partly illegible.

The copy checked against the f. 373 figures with key1.tsv at five places (dautant que cela me peut beaucoup ayder a me resouldre; faict pour faire continuer / que les ennemis pourroient faire contre moy; publie par dela du; plus dadvancement a mes affai[res]; de tant linsolence et audace de cet ennemy; dela a mondict service): no disagreement. The name the copy writes Vivac not settled on the figures. Reading texts/f373_reading.md: 0.924 clean sentences (85/92), explicit holes 0.978; state decoded, not read -> read (grade A).

outcome.method_basis: The content of both letters comes from contemporary clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 (BnF NAF 6984), located through the Harlay piece numbers and Berger de Xivrey; Tomokiyo's published key for Maisse's Cipher (1592) was applied to the 81 transcribed characters of f. 370, which match the Brienne copy.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b29), estimated: f. 373 now reads (about 3,500 groups, estimated from 53 lines and the copy's 4,062 letters) and the 80 transcribed groups of f. 370 read; the rest of f. 370 (about 550 groups by seg2.py) does not: about 3,580 of 4,130. Earlier: about 0.06 (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026, with f. 373 unread); 1.0 withdrawn.
outcome.notes: The content of both letters is settled by the contemporary clear copies. Group-by-group decipherment covers only the transcribed opening of f. 370, verified letter-for-letter; f. 373 is not transcribed. Split 14 Oct 2026: ff. 406 and 410, in a different cipher, are maisse1593.

texts.label: f. 370, S. Denis, 3 Nov 1592 (opening only)

reading_review.note: The transcribed opening (80 groups) decodes to one clean French sentence, identical letter for letter with the Brienne 13 fol. 102v clear copy ("Le Cardinal de Gondy aura passe pres de vous ..."). Only this opening is read; the rest of f. 370 (about 550 groups) is neither transcribed nor decoded, so the letter as a whole is not read.

texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse, his ambassador at Venice: Cardinal de Gondi has passed near Venice, shortly to be followed by the marquis de Pisany, going to the Pope in the name of the Catholics of the kingdom; the King presses Maisse not to leave his post, and reports that Mayenne has slipped into Paris and found the people weary of the war and against the introduction of the Spaniard. Only the opening is transcribed and deciphered here; the full text is the Brienne 13 clear copy (fol. 102v), not yet transcribed.

texts.label: f. 373, 7 Nov 1592 (clear copy Brienne 13 fol. 104v-106v transcribed; cipher checked at five places)
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letter of 4 October and will wait for the outcome of the Gondi and Pisany mission; urges the Venetian friends to help him with money and to work on the Pope, since only his person can preserve the Crown; approves Maisse's handling of the third-party (tiers parti) rumour; the duc de Retz has left without funding the Swiss, the League expects reinforcements while Parma is ill; Lesdiguières must be supported in Piedmont; Brèves has the Levant charge and Maisse is asked to stay at Venice a little longer. A clear postscript announces Joyeuse's defeat and death before Villemur.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b29): the letter's clear opening, close and postscript from the original (Gallica views 422-423), and the cipher from the contemporary clear copy in Brienne 13 fol. 104v-106v (views 109-112), transcribed for the first time; the copy checked against the cipher with Tomokiyo's key at five places (f. 373r ll. 3-4, three places mid-recto, f. 373v ll. 1 and 11), no disagreement. Body 0.924 clean sentences (85/92), explicit holes 0.978; holes are two single words of the copy, the date numeral and two lines of the clear postscript.
